{{Short description|Theory of quantum gravity}}
'''Hořava–Lifshitz gravity''' (or '''Hořava gravity''') is a theory of [[quantum gravity]] proposed by [[Petr Hořava (theorist)|Petr Hořava]] in 2009.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hořava |first=Petr |date=2009 |title=Quantum gravity at a Lifshitz point |journal=[[Physical Review D|Phys. Rev. D]] |volume=79 |issue=8 |article-number=084008 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.79.084008 |bibcode = 2009PhRvD..79h4008H |arxiv = 0901.3775 |s2cid=891685 }}</ref> It solves the problem of different concepts of time in [[quantum field theory]] and [[general relativity]] by treating the quantum concept as the more fundamental so that space and time are not equivalent ([[anisotropy|anisotropic]]) at high energy level. The relativistic concept of time with its [[Lorentz invariance]] emerges at large distances. The theory relies on the theory of [[foliation]]s to produce its [[causal structure]]. It is related to topologically massive gravity and the [[Cotton tensor]]. It is a possible [[UV completion]] of general relativity. Also, the speed of light goes to infinity at high energies. The novelty of this approach, compared to previous approaches to quantum gravity such as [[loop quantum gravity]], is that it uses concepts from [[condensed matter physics]] such as [[Quantum critical point|quantum critical phenomena]]. Hořava's initial formulation was found to have side-effects such as predicting very different results for a spherical [[Sun]] compared to a slightly non-spherical Sun, so others have modified the theory. Inconsistencies remain,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Charmousis |first1=C. |last2=Niz |first2=G. |last3=Padilla |first3=A. |last4=Saffin |first4=P. |date=2009 |title=Strong coupling in Horava gravity |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=2009 |issue=8 |page=070 |doi= 10.1088/1126-6708/2009/08/070|bibcode = 2009JHEP...08..070C |arxiv = 0905.2579 |s2cid=53363935 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Blas |first1=D. |last2=Pujolàs |first2=O. |last3=Sibiryakov |first3=S. |date=2009 |title=On the extra mode and inconsistency of Hořava gravity |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=2009 |issue=10 |page=029 |doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2009/10/029 |bibcode = 2009JHEP...10..029B |arxiv = 0906.3046 |s2cid=15368805 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Koyama |first1=Kazuya |last2=Arroja |first2=Frederico |date=2010 |title=Pathological behaviour of the scalar graviton in Hořava–Lifshitz gravity |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |volume=2010 |issue=3 |page=61 |doi=10.1007/JHEP03(2010)061 |bibcode = 2010JHEP...03..061K |arxiv = 0910.1998 |s2cid=119236847 }}</ref> though progress was made on the theory.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Wang |first=Anzhong |date=2017 |title=Hořava Gravity at a Lifshitz Point: A Progress Report |journal=International Journal of Modern Physics D |volume=26 |issue=7 |doi=10.1142/S0218271817300142 |bibcode =2017IJMPD..2630014W |arxiv =1701.06087 |s2cid=119258168 }} </ref> Nevertheless, observations of [[Gravitational wave|gravitational waves]] emitted by the neutron-star merger [[GW170817]] contravene predictions made by this ==Detailed balance condition==
Hořava originally imposed the theory to satisfy the detailed balance condition which considerably reduces the number of coupling constants in the action.
